{{Short description|Statistical measure of association}}
'''Digby's H''' is a measure of [[correlation|association]] for a 2 × 2 [[contingency table]]. It is a nonlinear transformation of the [[odds ratio]], proposed by P. G. N. Digby in 1983 as a computationally simple approximation to the [[tetrachoric correlation coefficient]], which otherwise requires iterative numerical estimation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Digby |first=P. G. N. |title=Approximating the tetrachoric correlation coefficient |journal=Biometrics |volume=39 |issue=3 |pages=753–757 |year=1983 |doi=10.2307/2531104}}</ref><ref name="WM">{{Cite journal |last=Warrens |first=Mathieu J. |title=On Association Coefficients for 2×2 Tables and Properties That Do Not Depend on the Marginal Distributions |journal=Psychometrika |volume=73 |issue=4 |pages=777–789 |year=2008 |doi=10.1007/s11336-008-9070-3}}</ref>

== Formula ==
For a 2×2 table of [[Binary variable|binary variables]] ''U'' and ''V'' with cell frequencies or proportions

{| class="wikitable"
! !! ''V'' = 0 !! ''V'' = 1
|-
| ''U'' = 0 || ''a'' || ''b''
|-
| ''U'' = 1 || ''c'' || ''d''
|}

the odds ratio is
:<math>\omega=\frac{ad}{bc}.</math>

Digby's H is defined as
:<math>H=\frac{(ad)^{3/4}-(bc)^{3/4}}{(ad)^{3/4}+(bc)^{3/4}}.</math>

Equivalently, in terms of the odds ratio,
:<math>H=\frac{\omega^{3/4}-1}{\omega^{3/4}+1}.</math>

== Properties ==
Digby's H ranges from −1 to 1. It equals zero under statistical independence of ''U'' and ''V'', since independence implies <math>ad=bc</math> and hence <math>\omega=1</math>. Positive values indicate positive association; negative values indicate negative association.

Because H depends on the table only through the ratio ''ad''/''bc'', it is invariant under multiplication of all four cell frequencies by the same positive constant, and — like any function of the odds ratio alone — its value is determined by ω independently of the row and column marginal totals.<ref name="WM" />

Digby's H belongs to a one-parameter family of odds-ratio transformations sometimes called generalized Yule coefficients,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bonett |first1=D. G. |last2=Price |first2=R. M. |title=Statistical Inference for Generalized Yule Coefficients in 2 × 2 Contingency Tables |journal=Sociological Methods & Research |volume=35 |issue=3 |pages=429–446 |year=2007 |doi=10.1177/0049124106292358}}</ref>
:<math>S_q=\frac{(ad)^q-(bc)^q}{(ad)^q+(bc)^q},</math>
where <math>q=1</math> gives [[Yule's Q]],
:<math>Q=\frac{ad-bc}{ad+bc},</math>
<math>q=1/2</math> gives [[Yule's Y]],
:<math>Y=\frac{\sqrt{ad}-\sqrt{bc}}{\sqrt{ad}+\sqrt{bc}},</math>
and <math>q=3/4</math> gives Digby's H. All members of this family are zero under independence and share the same sign as <math>ad-bc</math>.
